level_audit: PASS. Kartana 40 (0), Gastrodon-West 41 (+1), Lycanroc-Dusk 41 (+1), Archeops 41 (+1). All equal cap 42 + offset - 2.

attempts.note: Lost 2-6 with the Fire/Flying party carried over from Heidi. My error, not a difficulty spike: five of my six took Rock at 2x or 4x, and Archeops plus Lycanroc-Dusk both click Rock Slide. Archeops's Flying Gem Acrobatics OHKOed Weavile from 117 HP and the spread Rock Slide removed Togekiss and Charizard on the same turn.

Rebuilt entirely around Rock resistance (Steelix 0.25x, Swampert/Torterra/Garganacl 0.5x) with no Water move at all. Still cost five of six; the last eight turns were a Recover stall that only broke when Gastrodon ran out of PP.

strategy_checks.check: Kartana attacks and snowballs Attack with Beast Boost
strategy_checks.evidence: Kartana attacked on every turn it had (Smart Strike, Leaf Blade, Smart Strike) and its raw Attack is genuinely frightening - a 0.5x-resisted Leaf Blade still did 94 to a full-HP Heracross. But it never got a KO, so Beast Boost never triggered in either attempt. Focus Sash confirmed and it did survive a lethal Flamethrower at full HP in attempt 1.

strategy_checks.check: Storm Drain does not protect Kartana from Fire and does not redirect spread Water moves
strategy_checks.evidence: Attempt 1: Charizard's Flamethrower reached Kartana directly for 4x - Storm Drain correctly did not intervene against a Fire move. Neither party carried a Water move, so the redirection half was never exercised; the honest note is that a player who reads the dossier simply brings no Water attack and Gastrodon's signature ability becomes a blank.

strategy_checks.check: Lycanroc-Dusk offers Rock pressure and Accelerock priority
strategy_checks.evidence: Rock pressure: emphatically yes - its spread Rock Slide was the single most damaging thing either of Beau's fights produced, taking Togekiss and Charizard together in attempt 1. Accelerock was never used in either attempt; it preferred Rock Slide, Close Combat and Protect.

strategy_checks.check: Archeops gives a fast Flying Gem Acrobatics option
strategy_checks.evidence: Attempt 1 turn 3: Flying Gem Acrobatics OHKOed a 117-HP Weavile and the gem was consumed (item went to ITEM_NONE). It continued using Acrobatics at base power afterwards. Defeatist was visible in attempt 2 - once Archeops dropped to 45/125 its damage fell off sharply.

strategy_checks.check: Gastrodon's Icy Wind creates a useful next turn
strategy_checks.evidence: Attempt 1 turn 1 and turn 2, attempt 2 turn 7: spread Icy Wind put -1 Speed on both player battlers each time, which directly enabled Archeops and Lycanroc to move first in the turns that followed. This is the most consistently well-used move on the team.

protect_ledger.detail: Blocked a Swampert High Horsepower, which is 2x on Rock and was the single biggest threat to it on the board. It stayed at 125/125 and its partner's Earth Power KOed Garganacl on the same turn.

ai_notes: Target selection was good throughout: Gastrodon consistently aimed Earth Power at whichever of my bodies was 2x to it (Steelix, Garganacl) rather than the higher-HP neutral target, and the Icy Wind speed control was used proactively rather than as filler. The one questionable pattern is the endgame: from turn 8 to turn 16 Gastrodon used Recover every single turn while never attacking, against a Swampert that was out-damaging the heal by a small margin. That is a losing line - it spent eight turns falling from 139 to 0 without dealing a point of damage - but it is a close call rather than a clear scoring error, since its attacks could not have won the race either. Recorded here rather than as a defect.
level_decision: KEEP. One loss and one win, and the win still cost five of six Pokemon. Neither the raise condition (first-try win, 0-1 faints) nor the cut condition (three failed optimized attempts) is met. This is comfortably the hardest four-member route fight in the block.
cooler_note: The dossier's own verdict holds up and this run sharpens it. The Kartana/Gastrodon core is good and should stay - but the fight's real teeth turned out to be somewhere else entirely. Lycanroc-Dusk and Archeops both clicking Rock Slide into a doubles board is what actually won Beau a game, and Flying Gem Acrobatics OHKOing a healthy attacker is the moment I will remember, not Storm Drain. Meanwhile Storm Drain never did anything in either attempt, because the counterplay is simply 'bring no Water move', which costs a prepared player nothing. Two concrete suggestions, neither implemented: (1) the duplication the dossier flags is real - Beau's Archeops is byte-for-byte Travis's - and re-species or re-item of that slot is still the right call, but it should be replaced by something that punishes the Rock-resistant Ground/Steel answer this fight forces, not by another Flying attacker; (2) Gastrodon would be more interesting with a way to make Storm Drain matter against a player who brought no Water - Muddy Water or Surf on the team, so that the redirection protects a partner from the ALLY's spread move, would turn a dead ability into a real doubles interaction.
scope: Synthetic headless benchmark, not earned campaign play.
